  • Enhancer modules + gene sets + transcription factor enrichments and networks
    • 321: 3.5M+ DNaseI hypersensitive sites from Meuleman et al., (2020), which we overlay with H3K27ac activity and ChromHMM enhancer and promoter states to define active enhancers and promoters 336: 300 modules for active enhancers defined by k-centroids clustering. We provide cluster definitions (centers) and enhancer assignments to the clusters.

This directory contains trackhubs for epimap data, to be used on the UCSC or WUSTL browsers.

UCSC: Use .txt files 
WUSTL: Use .json files 

# Usage:
## WUSTL Epigenome Browser (Legacy):
1. Go to the WUSTL Browser: http://epigenomegateway.wustl.edu/legacy/?genome=hg19
2. Select the Tracks > Custom Tracks > Add new tracks > Datahub by upload > Upload File

## WUSTL Epigenome Browser (new):
1. Go to the WUSTL Browser: http://epigenomegateway.wustl.edu/browser/?genome=hg19
2. Select the Tracks > Remote Tracks > Add Remote Data Hub > Upload File

## UCSC Epigenome Browser:
Edit the following link with our hub location to connect the hub to the UCSC browser:

http://genome.ucsc.edu/cgi-bin/hgTracks?db=hg19&hubUrl=https://personal.broadinstitute.org/cboix/epimap/trackhubs/HUBNAME.txt

Analysis Datasets

Datasets corresponding to manuscript analyses can be found here and are summarized in the following table:

Dataset Files/Locations Description
Imputation metadata Tables in xlsx, tsv, summarized in html, and directory Extended tables matching manuscript analyses. For most use cases, the main metadata spreadsheet describes biosamples, attribution to ENCODE/Roadmap, and flagged samples.
DHS list website 3.5M+ DNaseI hypersensitive sites from Meuleman et al., (2020), which we overlay with H3K27ac activity and ChromHMM enhancer and promoter states to define active enhancers and promoters
Enh./Prom. locations directory, enhancers (0-ind), promoters (0-ind); enh. matrix hdf5, mtx; prom. matrix hdf5, mtx Enhancer, promoter, and dyadic element locations, enhancer/promoter + H3K27ac intersections as sparse matrices, and mappings from element lists to DHSs
Mark matrices H3K27ac, H3K4me1, H3K4me2, H3K4me3, H3K9ac, DNase-seq, column names, directory Dense mark activity matrices (3.5M+ DHSs x 833 biosamples) in hdf5 format. Loadable with h5py in Python or rhdf5 in R.
Enhancer modules assignments, centers, directory 300 modules for active enhancers defined by k-centroids clustering. We provide cluster definitions (centers) and enhancer assignments to the clusters.
Module enrichments archetype motifs, full motifs, GO terms Enrichments on 300 modules for GO terms (GREAT) and motifs (JASPAR 2018, HOCOMOCOv11, Jolma 2013 HT-SELEX). Motifs are split into archetypes according to Vierstra et al. (2020)
RNA-seq datasets Matrices (matrix-market format): all, full, pc, full + normalized, pc + normalized, id mapping 341 RNA-seq datasets from ENCODE matched to the unique epigenome identifiers. We provide all genes and only protein coding genes, as well as raw and quantile-normalized matrices, and the mapping between epigenome IDs and ENCODE accessions.
Gene-Enh. Links per-sample directory or per-group directory Per-sample and per-group gene-enhancer links by mark activity-by-gene expression correlation. Per-group links represent averages of all samples from a specific sample group.
GWAS enrichments (original) See note below: Original enr. (tsv (1%), tsv (0.1%), Rda); summary figs. and GWAS loci figs.; enh. (tsv, Rda) and links (tsv, Rda) GWAS enrichments resources, including enrichments, summary figures, GWAS loci figures (all plotted links in GWAS loci are given per-folder as either tsv.gz or Rda files), and lead SNP-overlapping enhancers and links.
GWAS enrichments (revised) Revised enrichments for epigenomes (tsv, Rds); modules (tsv, Rds); and tree nodes (tsv); summary figs. and GWAS loci figs.; enh. (tsv, Rda) and links (tsv, Rda) GWAS enrichments resources, including enrichments, summary figures, GWAS loci figures (all plotted links in GWAS loci are given per-folder as either tsv.gz or Rda files), and lead SNP-overlapping enhancers and links.

Note: We have updated the site to correct for two mistakes in the GWAS enrichment analysis:

  1. The first mistake was that we calculated the enrichment in the wrong direction: instead of calculating the enrichment of SNPs in biosample enhancers as was previously done in Roadmap, we mistakenly calculated the enrichment of enhancers in GWAS lead SNPs. This led to double-counting SNPs and inflated enrichment statistics in the case of multiple nearby enhancers within 2.5kb of the same lead SNP, which were all counted as independently overlapping the same SNP, when in fact the multiple overlaps came from their genomic clustering in the same locus.
  2. The second mistake was that our FDR procedure only controlled for inflation due to multiple enhancers proximal to the same SNP, but not for the multiple hypothesis testing across many tissue-trait combinations, and thus our original reported statistics correspond to nominal P-values rather than FDR-corrected P-values. Empirical FDR estimates for all of our original enrichment analyses are: 38% for epigenomes, 80% for modules, 55% for tree nodes.
